title: Lesson 9: Fighting for Purity
description: Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw that as two people draw near to God, they draw near to each other. Temptation pulls the opposite way, away from God and away from the people you love. This lesson is about purity, which means guarding your body, your eyes, and your mind, whether you are married or single.
Temptation will arrive. The question is what you do in the first moment, and the answer starts with grace.

blocks.alt: King David, fully clothed, alone on his palace roof overlooking the city, with his royal robe and crown set aside

blocks.title: The View from the Roof
blocks.text:
David was Israel's greatest king, a man after God's own heart. One spring, when kings went out to battle, David stayed home. Late one afternoon he walked on his palace roof and saw a woman bathing. Instead of turning away, he kept looking. He learned she was Bathsheba, the wife of one of his soldiers, and he sent messengers and took her.

When she became pregnant, David tried to hide what he had done. When hiding failed, he arranged for her husband Uriah to be killed in battle. One moment on a roof became a string of choices, and the pit got deeper.

David stayed hidden until God sent the prophet Nathan to confront him. Only then did he say, "I have sinned against the LORD."
Years earlier, Joseph faced the same moment as a slave in Potiphar's house, with nothing and no power, and he ran. David had everything and stayed.
<sup>10</sup>The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.
9.1 - When temptation comes, what is normally going on when you fall, and what has helped you run away from it?
At First Thought
Purity starts in the heart. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said:

<sup>27</sup>You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.' <sup>28</sup>But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
A passing thought is not a sin. Jesus Himself was tempted. A tempting thought is a knock at the door. Lust is opening the door and letting it stay.
David's fall did not begin when he sent the messengers. It began on the roof, in the moment he decided to keep looking. So when the thought knocks, run.
R-U-N from Sin
Paul wrote to young Christians in Corinth, a city full of sexual temptation. He told them to RUN.

17But he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him. 18Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. 19Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, 20for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

When we flee from sin we RUN away. When temptation arrives, you have a choice: run toward life, or fall toward the pit. When you get close to the line you should never cross, it is time to RUN the other way. Leave the party, turn off the screen, or call a friend for help.

R is for Remember the Cross. Temptation says your body is yours to use however you want. Paul says you are not your own, because you were bought with a price. Count the cost. Your forgiveness was bought with the life of God's own Son. Never take forgiveness for granted.
Grace does not whisper, "Go ahead, you will be forgiven anyway."
<sup>1</sup>What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? <sup>2</sup>By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?

You are forgiven, fully and freely. But grace does not just cancel your debt. It makes you new, so you do not keep on sinning. You are not fighting for purity so God will let you into His family. You are fighting because you are already in it, loved by a Father who paid everything to set you free.
9.2 - When has grace felt like permission instead of power, and what would change if you believed it could actually help you run?

U is for United with God. Paul says something startling: you are joined to the Lord, one spirit with Him. Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. You are not your own, because you were bought with a price.
David thought the roof was private. It never was. There is no secret sin, because there is no moment God is not present with you.

But that same presence is your power. You are not fighting temptation on your own strength, and you are not fighting it alone. The God who lives in you is stronger than what is pulling at you. The cross did not only buy your forgiveness when you fail. It bought you the power to run.
N is for Need others. Sin grows best in hiding, just as it did for David. Notice all the 2s in 2 Timothy 2:22, and let them remind you to run with another.
22So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

A true friend comes close. Nathan went to David instead of talking about him. He tells the truth. Nathan loved David too much to let him keep hiding. He points to grace. When David said, "I have sinned against the LORD," Nathan answered, "The LORD also has put away your sin" (2 Samuel 12:13). Ask God for your Nathan, and be ready to be one for someone else.
9.3 - What is one habit or boundary you can establish to better protect your mind and heart?
When You Fall, Repent
Maybe you read David's story and thought, "That is me." Look at what David did when Nathan confronted him. He did not make excuses. He repented, and later he wrote:
<sup>5</sup>I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not cover my iniquity; I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD," and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.

Repentance is turning back to God. Repent by reflecting honestly on what pulled you away, and let remorse lead you to confess your sin. Then trust that God forgives you. Next, make a plan that will help you fight sin and ask someone to walk along with you.
9.4 - Who could be your Nathan, and how would you invite them into this part of your life?
Lesson 9 Review
David did not run. His fall began with a look and grew in hiding, until God sent Nathan with the truth and David turned back.
Purity does not earn God's love. It protects a heart that already belongs to Him. So when temptation arrives, RUN. Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others.
And the cross does more than forgive you when you fall. Jesus came down into the pit to get you out, and the God who lives in you now gives you the power to run.
Next, you will come to the table Jesus set for His people, where the price of your forgiveness is on display.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
